prompt:
Animate this lineup of ten game enemies as ONE attack, all ten at the same time, each attacking in place. The camera is fixed and does not move, zoom or pan. Left and right in this description are the screen's left and right. Forward is screen right: every character faces screen right and its target is an enemy standing just outside the picture to the right of its own position, at the height of its chest, one body length in front of it.
Every beat, for each character: the body stays near-side-view facing screen right with the head looking forward at the target; both feet (or all four paws) stay planted on the same ground line as in the image, the feet never slide; each character stays exactly where it stands in the image, inside its own cell, and never moves into another character's space; the ten never touch or overlap; every character keeps its own size, the small ones stay small and the large ones stay large; every character, the big ones included, stays completely inside the picture in every frame, with all of its weapon and cloak.
Five characters are melee fighters and each attacks with one continuous move in a vertical plane flat to the screen, from the hips or the shoulders: the character first coils back away from the target toward screen left while its weapon rises up and back, then it turns toward the target and brings the weapon straight down in a big arc in front of the body, toward screen right and down, through the target, ending low in front of the character, and leans forward into the blow. The Frostbite Raider swings its one-handed axe, the Frost Knight swings its broad sword, the Glacier Gladiator swings its giant ice maul overhead and smashes it down, the Frost Warlord raises its two-handed greatsword overhead with both hands and brings it down. The Frost Wolf rears up on its hind legs with both front paws raised, then slams both front paws and its jaws down toward the target.
The Icicle Stalker is an assassin and attacks with a fast low slash. He holds exactly ONE short curved ice sword, in a REVERSE GRIP, and it stays the only weapon in every frame: no second sword, no copy of the blade, no extra blade appears in his other hand or anywhere. Crouched low and leaning forward, he draws the hand that holds the sword back beside his hip, the blade running back along the outside of the forearm, then lunges forward low and sweeps the sword in one short level slash across the front of his body at chest height toward screen right, his other hand open and empty for balance, and holds the end of the slash with that one sword still in the same hand and his other hand still empty.
Three characters are ranged attackers and only perform the body motion of the attack; they shoot and cast nothing. The Rime Archer holds the bow out level toward the target, draws the bowstring back to its cheek with the other hand, and holds the aim; no arrow is released. The Snow Witch raises her crystal staff up and back, then thrusts it straight forward toward the target at chest height with both hands, the crystal pointing at the target, and holds it. The Blizzard Shaman raises his bone totem high and shakes it once, then thrusts it straight forward toward the target at chest height and holds it. In every frame the bow, the bowstring, the staff, the crystal and the totem stay exactly as drawn in the image: no arrow, no ice, no snow, no frost, no mist, no spark, no light, no beam, no ball, no projectile, no blast and no glow leaves them or appears in front of them. The whole space in front of each of these three, from its weapon to the edge of its own cell, stays empty flat magenta background in every frame.
The Spear Hurler throws its javelin in one overhand throw, in these beats: first it leans back with its weight on the back foot, its throwing arm bent and drawn back behind its head with the javelin held along its shoulder, the tip pointing forward at the target and slightly up, its other arm stretched out forward pointing at the target; then its hips and shoulders turn toward the target, its front foot steps forward and plants, and its throwing arm whips forward over the shoulder; at the full extension of the arm the javelin leaves the hand and flies straight toward screen right at chest height, level and fast, and leaves the picture at the right edge; the throwing arm follows through forward and down and the pose is held with the throwing hand open and empty, the other arm still pointing at the target. Nothing else leaves the Spear Hurler, and the javelin never touches another character.
After the blow, the slash, the throw or the gesture lands the move ends and the pose is held: no return to the starting stance, no second strike. No motion trail, no slash arc, no swoosh, no streak and no afterimage is drawn behind any weapon or limb. Every character keeps its own design, colours and outline exactly as in the image; the crystals and the glow stay on its own body and never drift to another character; no character has a tail except the Frost Wolf.
The flat solid pure magenta background stays unchanged and fixed in every frame: no scenery, no ground, no shadows, no extra effects, no text, no grid, no camera shake.
